learning_objective: The learner will explain how the three benchmark stages chain by opening each of 7 elements of the pipeline and then answering 4 questions about what starts from what, with at least 3 of 4 correct.
specification:
Type: workflow **sim-id:** benchmark-stage-pipeline
**Library:** Mermaid
**Status:** Specified
**Template:** https://github.com/dmccreary/learning-graphs/tree/main/docs/sims/book-build-workflow-pipeline
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** explain
**Learning Objective:** The learner will explain how the three benchmark stages chain by opening each of 7 elements of the pipeline and then answering 4 questions about what starts from what, with at least 3 of 4 correct. **Prerequisites:** pipeline stage, stage chaining, benchmark workspace template, per-chapter generation run, run time limit, run event stream (all defined in the sections above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner opens all 7 elements to read their descriptions, then answers 4 questions, each by choosing one element, before any answer is revealed. A choice is correct when it equals the Correct element column. Mastery is 3 of 4 correct on the first attempt. Opening an element is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Every stage starts from the template. (2) Stage 3 is one run for the whole book. (3) A run that hits its time limit loses what it wrote. (4) A run can change its starting directory. **Instructional Rationale:** Understand-level explaining of a chained process needs the learner to place inputs and outputs, so each element's description names where it starts from and what it leaves, and the questions ask the learner to locate a fact in that structure. **Content:** The seven elements, in order, with the description shown when an element is opened: | # | Element | Description shown | |---|---|---| | 1 | Template workspace | The fixed starting directory with the course description. It is copied for each run and never changed. | | 2 | Stage 1 run | Runs the learning-graph skill on a copy of the template, with a 150-minute limit. | | 3 | Stage 1 output | The run directory holding the seven required files of the learning graph. | | 4 | Stage 2 run | Runs the chapter-structure skill on a copy of the stage 1 output, with a 2-hour limit. | | 5 | Stage 2 output | The run directory holding one directory and outline per chapter. | | 6 | Stage 3 runs | One run per chapter, each on a copy of the book so far, with a 90-minute limit each. | | 7 | Finished book | The run directory after the last chapter, which is the book the model wrote. | The four questions: | # | Question shown to the learner | Correct element | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Which element is the starting point of stage 2? | Stage 1 output | Each stage starts from a copy of the previous stage's output. | | 2 | Which element runs once for each chapter? | Stage 3 runs | The chapter skill is run once per chapter so each gets its own timing and limit. | | 3 | Which element must never be changed by a run? | Template workspace | It is copied for each run, so every run starts from the same input. | | 4 | Which element holds the seven required files of the learning graph? | Stage 1 output | The seven files are the required output of stage 1. | **Provenance:** The elements and limits come from the benchmark's runner and prompts and from the sections of this chapter above. The questions are synthetic, written for this exercise, and the sim labels them "synthetic example". **Rules:** Elements may be opened in any order. The questions are asked in the fixed order 1 to 4, each allows one final choice among the seven elements, and exactly one element is correct for each question. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner opens each of the 7 elements of the pipeline and reads its description. The questions unlock after all seven have been opened. 2. The learner reads question 1 and chooses an element, then confirms. 3. The sim shows the correct element and the Why text, and marks the question correct or incorrect. 4. The learner repeats for questions 2 to 4. After question 4 the sim shows the score and the misconception behind each miss. **Feedback:** Four questions, fixed order, one confirmed choice each, no second attempt. Correct: "Correct" followed by the Why text. Incorrect: "Not quite" followed by the correct element and the Why text. The final score reads "n of 4 correct". **Starting State:** The pipeline is shown with no element opened, and the instruction on screen is "Open each element to see what it does". **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter states that each stage starts from a copy of the previous stage's output, that the template is never changed, that stage 3 runs once per chapter, and that the limits are 150 minutes, 2 hours, and 90 minutes per chapter.
